name: Downstream

angles.text: Keeping Eastvale Logging Camp supplied with tools helps its timber reach Stormwind and Elwynn's settlements.

faq.answer: Ormin Pelford asks for help near Eastvale Logging Camp. He is a laborer whose supply wagon overturned in the river while he was hauling goods from a trading post.
Ormin Pelford lost a Waterlogged Axe, a Waterlogged Saw, and a Waterlogged Toolbox. They fell into the river when his wagon tipped over.
faq.q: What supplies were lost in the water?

faq.answer: The crates and tools drifted downstream along the river south of Eastvale Logging Camp in eastern Elwynn Forest.
faq.q: Where did the supplies wash up?

faq.answer: Ormin Pelford cannot face the riverbanks alone, where river murlocs and forest wolves prowl near the cargo.
faq.q: Why can't Ormin Pelford retrieve the supplies himself?

faq.answer: Aggressive murlocs claim the downstream riverbanks, and wolves prowl nearby. Salvage is dangerous there.
faq.q: What dangers lurk along the riverbanks?

faq.answer: The axes, saws, and toolboxes are essential to the woodsmen at Eastvale Logging Camp. They provide raw timber for Elwynn Forest and Stormwind.
faq.q: Why are these tools important to Eastvale?

sections.body: Laborer Ormin Pelford was bringing a shipment back from a local trading post when his wagon tipped near Eastvale Logging Camp. Its gear spilled into the river, and the current swept it downstream before he could secure it. Without the woodworking tools, the loggers face delays in their timber work.
sections.title: A Mishap on the Road

sections.body: Ormin Pelford's lost cargo lies along banks where murlocs and wolves roam. Aggressive murlocs claim the muddy shoals downstream, while predatory wolves prowl the surrounding woods. Ormin cannot face those dangers alone. He needs hardy travelers to search the riverbanks, recover the submerged saw, axe, and toolbox, and bring them back safely.
sections.title: Perils Along the Riverbank

summary: Near Eastvale Logging Camp, Ormin Pelford's wagon has overturned, and the river has carried his woodworking tools downstream. Murlocs and wolves guard the banks where they lie.
